title: The Lasting State: 着
description: Verb + 着 for a state that continues (门开着, 穿着), doing one thing while doing another (笑着说), and 'there is … lying / hanging' (墙上挂着).

points.title: Verb + 着: lasting state
points.summary: 着 (zhe) shows a state that continues: the door is (standing) open, she's wearing ….
points.body:
- 门一直开**着**.
- 她穿**着**一件红色的衣服.

points.title: V1 + 着 + V2: while / in a … way
points.summary: V1着 describes how the main action is done: 笑着说 (said smiling), 走着去 (go on foot).
points.body:
- 他笑**着**说: '没关系.'
- 我们走**着**去吧.
examples: He said with a smile: 'Never mind.'

points.title: Place + verb + 着 + thing
points.summary: Describes what is (lying / hanging / sitting) somewhere: 墙上挂着一张地图.
points.body:
- 墙上挂**着**一张地图.
- 桌子上放**着**一本书.
examples: There's a map hanging on the wall.

notes: 一直开了 isn't grammatical — 一直 needs a lasting state.
questions.translation: The classroom door has been open the whole time — nobody closed it.

questions.prompt: {她|tā}{穿|chuān}（　）{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóngsè}{的|de}{衣服|yīfu}，{很|hěn}{好看|hǎokàn}。
questions.translation: She's wearing red — it looks lovely.
He said with a smile: 'Never mind.'

notes: 着 can't come before a verb.
着 follows the first verb (走).
questions.translation: Let's walk there — it isn't far.

notes: 挂在 needs a place after it.
questions.translation: There's a map of China hanging on the wall.

notes: In this pattern the place comes first.
questions.translation: There's a book on the table.
